questions.q: What does the step chain of an escalator do?
o: Links the steps and drives them around the loop
Drives the handrail only
Holds the balustrade panels in place
Guides feet off the steps at the comb
questions.ref: ASME A17.1 elevator and escalator terminology; Strakosch, The Vertical Transportation Handbook
questions.n: The steps are pinned to two chains that run over sprockets at each end, driven by the drive unit.

questions.q: What is true about escalators and accessible routes?
o: Every escalator is wheelchair-accessible
An escalator does not by itself give a required accessible route
An escalator counts as a ramp
An escalator can replace an elevator if run slowly
questions.n: Wheelchair users cannot ride escalators. BP 344 requires an alternative route such as an elevator or ramp.

questions.q: Why are the top and bottom landings of an escalator critical?
o: The steps move at their fastest speed there
The truss is at its deepest point there
Riders step between the still floor and the moving steps
The handrail stops moving there for safety
questions.ref: ASME A17.1 elevator and escalator terminology; Strakosch, The Vertical Transportation Handbook
questions.n: Most falls happen at the landings. The comb plate, flat steps and run-off space all serve that transition.

questions.q: What is the balustrade of an escalator?
o: The housing of the drive motor
The track that guides the step rollers
The toothed plate at the landing
The side enclosure that carries the handrail
questions.ref: ASME A17.1 elevator and escalator terminology; Strakosch, The Vertical Transportation Handbook
questions.n: Balustrades are glass or metal panels along each side. The handrail runs along their top.

questions.q: What does the escalator truss do?
o: Spans between floors and carries the whole mechanism
Drives the steps around the loop at each end
Guides feet off the moving steps at the landing
Gives riders a moving handhold along the incline
questions.ref: ASME A17.1 elevator and escalator terminology; Strakosch, The Vertical Transportation Handbook
questions.n: The truss is a steel frame resting on supports at each floor. Its depth and support points come from the maker.

questions.q: What does the escalator drive unit do?
o: Guides the step rollers along the track
Powers the step chain and handrail
Carries the riders' weight to the floor
Stops the steps at the landing comb
questions.ref: ASME A17.1 elevator and escalator terminology; Strakosch, The Vertical Transportation Handbook
questions.n: A motor and gearbox, usually at the upper landing, turn the drive sprockets.

questions.q: How are escalators placed in a parallel arrangement?
o: At right angles to each other on each floor
Alternating direction and stacked in a zigzag
Side by side, usually one up and one down
End to end in a single long run
questions.ref: ASME A17.1 elevator and escalator terminology; Strakosch, The Vertical Transportation Handbook
questions.n: Parallel units are easy to see and suit heavy two-way traffic. The crisscross layout stacks units in alternating directions.

questions.q: Where is the comb plate of an escalator?
o: At mid-run, halfway up the incline
Under the handrail where it turns at the newel
In the machine space under the upper landing
At each landing, where steps meet the fixed floor
questions.ref: ASME A17.1 elevator and escalator terminology; Strakosch, The Vertical Transportation Handbook
questions.n: The comb teeth mesh with the step grooves to lift feet off the steps.

questions.q: Under the BP 344 IRR, what is the minimum escalator tread width?
o: S800 type (804 mm)
S600 type (604 mm)
questions.ref: BP 344 Revised IRR (2024), Appendix A, Sec. 10.2
questions.n: The 2024 IRR requires at least an S800 tread, 804 mm wide, so a rider can stand with a companion or bag.

questions.q: Which planning statement about escalators and elevators is correct?
o: Elevators are always slower than escalators, at any height
Escalators suit nearby levels; elevators suit far-apart floors
Escalators suit direct trips to floors far apart
Escalators can stop at any floor a rider requests
questions.ref: ASME A17.1 elevator and escalator terminology; Strakosch, The Vertical Transportation Handbook
questions.n: Escalators carry heavy continuous flows over a few floors. Elevators give selective service over many.

questions.q: What is the moving handrail of an escalator for?
o: Driving the steps around the loop
Guiding the step rollers on the track
A handhold that moves at about step speed
Covering the gap beside the moving steps
questions.ref: ASME A17.1 elevator and escalator terminology; Strakosch, The Vertical Transportation Handbook
questions.n: If the handrail runs slower than the steps, riders get pulled off balance. A monitor stops the unit if the speeds differ.

questions.q: What do the escalator tracks do?
o: Store the spare steps under the landing
Carry the handrail around the newel end
Hold the comb plate in place at the landing
Guide the step rollers so the steps form stairs
questions.ref: ASME A17.1 elevator and escalator terminology; Strakosch, The Vertical Transportation Handbook
questions.n: Two sets of tracks, one for each pair of rollers, hold each step level while its position changes along the loop.

questions.q: Why must escalator floor openings be coordinated early?
o: The truss, supports, landings and clearances all depend on them
The openings affect only the finishes around them
Escalators rest on the floor and need no supports
The opening size is the same for every model
questions.ref: ASME A17.1 elevator and escalator terminology; Strakosch, The Vertical Transportation Handbook
questions.n: Openings cut through slabs and beams and need headroom and run-off space at each end.

questions.q: Why are escalators common in malls and transit stations?
o: They serve far-apart floors directly
They move large, continuous flows between nearby levels
They satisfy accessibility rules on their own
They need no floor openings
questions.ref: ASME A17.1 elevator and escalator terminology; Strakosch, The Vertical Transportation Handbook
questions.n: An escalator can carry several thousand people an hour with no waiting.

questions.q: What is the skirt panel of an escalator?
o: The glass balustrade panel below the handrail
The moving handrail belt
The fixed side panel right beside the moving steps
The floor plate at the landing
questions.ref: ASME A17.1 elevator and escalator terminology; Strakosch, The Vertical Transportation Handbook
questions.n: The steps slide past the skirt with a small gap, so it is a known entrapment point and has deflector brushes.

o: A fixed emergency stair
An inclined moving walk with a flat surface
A hydraulic lift for goods
A power-driven, continuously moving stairway between levels
questions.ref: ASME A17.1 elevator and escalator terminology; Strakosch, The Vertical Transportation Handbook
questions.n: An escalator is a loop of linked steps on tracks that form stairs on the incline.

questions.q: What happens at the escalator's return station?
o: The step chain turns around to run back underneath
The handrail drive motor is housed there
The emergency stop button is located there
Passengers get on and off the escalator there
questions.ref: ASME A17.1 elevator and escalator terminology; Strakosch, The Vertical Transportation Handbook
questions.n: The steps flip over at each end and return upside down under the truss.

questions.q: What is a crisscross escalator arrangement?
o: All units run side by side in the same direction on each floor
Up and down units alternate, so riders board the next flight at once
Units are placed end to end in one long, straight run
One escalator per floor runs up and down in turns
questions.ref: ASME A17.1 elevator and escalator terminology; Strakosch, The Vertical Transportation Handbook
questions.n: Crisscross layouts are compact and keep riders moving from floor to floor. Parallel layouts make riders walk around to the next flight.
